findings.title: Add/remove members read group_id but the route only sets id
findings.body: add_members and remove_member load the group with params.require(:group_id). The new routes are member routes on resources :groups (DELETE/PUT /admin/groups/:id/members), so Rails only populates params[:id]. The client calls /admin/groups/:id/members.json and does not send group_id in the body. Every add or remove therefore raises ParameterMissing (400) and membership changes never persist. Controller specs pass group_id directly and never hit the router, so they hide this. Use params[:id] (and fix the automatic-group spec, which calls remove_member with PUT instead of DELETE).

findings.title: Member row template looks up member and automatic on the wrong object
findings.body: group.hbs renders members with {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}} and no block. That item view's context is the user, and the each-block param member is not in scope in group_member.hbs. {{member.username}} and {{avatar member}} therefore resolve against the user (no member property), so names and avatars render blank, and {{action "removeMember" member}} passes undefined so removal cannot work. {{#unless automatic}} is also evaluated on the user, not the group, so it is always true and automatic groups still show a remove control. The template should use the item context (username / this) and the group's automatic flag from the parent controller.

findings.title: Removing a member bypasses Group#remove
findings.body: add_members still calls group.add(user), but remove_member does group.users.delete(user_id) and then group.save. Association delete skips Group#remove, which is what previously updated membership (user_count and other callbacks such as primary group). After a successful delete the join row is gone but denormalized group state can stay stale, so admin counts and anything keyed off user_count are wrong until some other process recomputes them. Call the same removal API used before (group.remove) instead of users.delete.

findings.title: Creating a group drops alias_level
findings.body: The admin form shows the alias-level combo before the group has an id, and Group#asJSON sends alias_level on POST /admin/groups. create only assigns name and visible (params[:visible] == "true") and never reads alias_level. The chosen level is discarded; it is only stored if the admin later hits update. Set alias_level on create the same way update does.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when the count divides evenly
findings.body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is one page too many whenever user_count is a positive multiple of limit (50 members at limit 50 shows 2/2). showingLast stays false on the real last page, and next() then sets offset to user_count, so findMembers loads an empty page. Use ceil(user_count / limit), and do not advance offset to user_count.

findings.title: Members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit
findings.body: limit is (params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no upper bound, and offset is not clamped to >= 0. This action is public (only ensure_can_see!). A caller can pass a huge limit and force a full member serialization in one response, which is the opposite of the pagination this change adds and is an easy load amplifier. Cap limit (and reject negative offset/limit) before the query.

findings.title: GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed
findings.body: members used to render a JSON array of GroupUserSerializer objects. It now returns {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}. Any client still expecting the array (plugins, API consumers) will break, and this PR adds no request spec for the new contract. Document the break or keep a compatible shape if this endpoint is public.
